verses.text: After that, Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Let my people go, so that they can hold a feast for me in the desert.'"
Pharaoh said, "Who is the LORD, that I should obey him and let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, and I will not let Israel go."

Then they said, "The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go on a three-day journey into the desert to offer sacrifices to the LORD our God. If we do not, he may strike us with disease or with the sword."
But the king of Egypt said, "Moses and Aaron, why are you taking the people away from their work? Get back to work!"
Pharaoh said, "Look, there are now so many of your people in the land, and you are stopping them from working."
That same day Pharaoh gave orders to the slave masters and the foremen over the people.
He said, "Do not give the people straw for making bricks any more, like you did before. Let them go and gather their own straw.
But make them make the same number of bricks as before. Do not lower the number. They are lazy. That is why they are crying out, 'Let us go and offer sacrifices to our God.'
Make the work harder for them, so that they are kept busy and pay no attention to lies."
So the slave masters and the foremen went out and said to the people, "This is what Pharaoh says: 'I will not give you any more straw.
Go and get your own straw wherever you can find it. But your work will not be reduced at all.'"
So the people spread out all over Egypt to gather stubble to use for straw.
The slave masters kept pushing them, saying, "Finish your work for each day, just as you did when you had straw!"
Pharaoh's slave masters beat the Israelite foremen they had put in charge. They asked them, "Why have you not made the same number of bricks yesterday and today as you did before?"
Then the Israelite foremen went to Pharaoh and cried out, "Why are you treating your servants like this?
We are given no straw, yet we are told, 'Make bricks!' Your servants are being beaten, but the fault is with your own people."
Pharaoh said, "You are lazy! Lazy! That is why you keep saying, 'Let us go and offer sacrifices to the LORD.'
Now get back to work! You will not be given any straw, but you must still make the full number of bricks."
The Israelite foremen saw that they were in trouble when they were told, "You must not reduce the number of bricks you make each day."
When they left Pharaoh, they found Moses and Aaron waiting to meet them.
They said to them, "May the LORD look at what you have done and judge you! You have made Pharaoh and his officials hate us. You have put a sword in their hands to kill us!"
Moses went back to the LORD and said, "Lord, why have you brought trouble on this people? Why did you send me?
Ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has treated this people badly. And you have not saved your people at all!"
